children: The carmaker is aiming to slash expenses by $9 bln over four years, according to Reuters, cutting less deep than rival Nissan. CEO Toshihiro Mibe may be doing enough to return Honda’s auto unit operating margin to past highs, but performance would still lag Chinese rival BYD.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Katrina Hamlin on Bluesky and LinkedIn.

Honda Motor is aiming to cut 1.5 trillion yen ($9.4 billion) in costs at its carmaking business over the four financial years from April this year to the end of March 2030, Reuters reported on September 2, citing internal documents and one person familiar with ‌the matter.

The company has also instructed suppliers to drastically reduce their prices, the report added. Honda is ‌aiming to ⁠reduce costs by 30% in three key parts categories: pressed and forged components, electrical parts, and parts related to software-defined vehicles (SDVs), according to the documents.

In a written response to questions from Reuters, a Honda spokesperson declined to comment on specific cost-reduction targets or details of discussions with suppliers. The automaker was working with suppliers globally to improve competitiveness and reduce costs, including through the use of standardised parts, the spokesperson said.
